label: NCSA QP (Illinois)
source: Showerman et al., 'QP: A Heterogeneous Multi-Accelerator Cluster', LCI 2009 (impact.crhc.illinois.edu/shared/papers/lci09_paper.pdf); Kindratenko et al. Cluster 2009
note: 16 nodes x 4 FX 5600 = 64 G80 (128 SP @1.35 GHz = 518 GF). Paper quotes 23 TF SP (MAD-only). Used 'since 2007' for CUDA courses; exact month unknown. Upgraded into NCSA AC in 2009. Earliest CUDA-era GPU compute cluster found; Vendor peak FP32 for G80/GT200 counts MAD+MUL dual-issue (3 flop/clk/SP); MAD-only = x2/3

label: Mole-9.7 (IPE CAS)
source: CAS press release 2009-04-20 (cas.cn/xw/zyxw/yw/200904/t20090420_2313689.shtml): Feb 2008 GPU system 120 TF SP peak; HPCwire 2009-11-03: 126 HP workstations, 200 Tesla C870
note: 200 x C870 (128 SP @1.35 GHz = 518 GF) = 104 TF; CAS states 120 TF peak SP, used here. Upgraded with GTX 295s in early 2009 and folded into Mole-8.7 (Mar 2009)

label: TSUBAME 1.2
source: TOP500 Nov 2008 #29/30 (top500.org/lists/top500/list/2008/11/); Tokyo Tech news 2009-07-31; GSIC TSUBAME ESJ vol.1: S1070 4 GPUs @1.44 GHz 1036 GFLOPS each, 680 GPUs on 340 nodes
note: 170 S1070 = 680 T10 x 1036.8 GF. First GPU-accelerated system on TOP500 (Nov 2008; NVIDIA/HPCwire/Ars). Upgrade done Oct-Nov 2008 while live. End = TSUBAME 2.0 start (approx). Vendor peak FP32 for G80/GT200 counts MAD+MUL dual-issue (3 flop/clk/SP); MAD-only = x2/3

label: NCSA Lincoln
source: Kindratenko et al., 'GPU Clusters for HPC', IEEE Cluster 2009 (Table I: 192 nodes, 384 GPU chips @1.44 GHz); NCSA 2011-05-18 Forge release (replaces Lincoln, production by July 1 2011)
note: 96 S1070 = 384 T10 x 1036.8 GF. Installed Oct 2008, production Feb 2009 (Jacobsen et al. AIAA 2010). Never listed on TOP500 as GPU system. Vendor peak FP32 for G80/GT200 counts MAD+MUL dual-issue (3 flop/clk/SP); MAD-only = x2/3

label: NCSA AC (Illinois)
source: Kindratenko et al., IEEE Cluster 2009, Table I: 32 nodes, 128 GPU chips @1.30 GHz; production 2009
note: 128 x 933 GF (C1060-class). Start month approx (paper: 'went into production in 2009'); end date is a placeholder, no retirement date found. Vendor peak FP32 for G80/GT200 counts MAD+MUL dual-issue (3 flop/clk/SP); MAD-only = x2/3

label: Mole-8.7 (IPE CAS)
chip_type: Mixed: GTX 295, GTX 280, Tesla C1060, Radeon HD 4870 X2
source: CAS press release 2009-04-20 (4 subsystems 450+150+200+200 TF SP, linked March 2009, >1 PF SP); Bulletin of CAS 2011 no.4 ('1000多块GPU卡'); Li et al., Chinese Sci Bull 54(20) 2009 doi:10.1360/972009-1347 (953-GPU run, 945 TF SP peak)
note: 4 sub-clusters (IPE x2, Lenovo, Sugon) joined via GigE/IB - a federated cluster, not one tightly coupled machine. chips = 953 GPU chips used in full-system LBM run (232 GTX295 + 137 HD4870X2 + 153 GTX280 + 62 C1060, 945 TF); full system >1000 cards, ~1 PF SP. Largest GPU system Mar-Oct 2009 if counted. End is a placeholder (still cited 2011; Mole-8.5 networked with it Apr 2010). Vendor peak FP32 for G80/GT200 counts MAD+MUL dual-issue (3 flop/clk/SP); MAD-only = x2/3 | EXCLUDED: four linked sub-clusters, not one machine (see definition)

label: GENCI-CCRT Titane (CEA)
source: Ter@tec 2009-06-24 (Bull machine installed April 2009); CSCI Sept 2009 slides (48 Tesla servers x 4 GPUs, 192 TF SP); Le Monde Informatique 2008-04-18; TOP500 Nov 2009 #52 lists CPU part only
note: 48 S1070 = 192 T10, CCRT quotes 192 TF SP. Opened to GENCI users summer 2009. End approx = Airain in service 09/2012 (no Titane stop date found)

label: DEGIMA (Nagasaki Univ.)
source: Hamada & Nitadori, SC10 Gordon Bell finalist '190 TFlops astrophysical N-body simulation on a cluster of GPUs' (144 nodes, 576 GT200); BU PASI bio: 288 GTX295 acquired Aug 2009; SC09 Gordon Bell price/perf prize
note: 288 GTX 295 cards = 576 GT200 x 894 GF (240 SP @1.242 GHz x3). Consumer cards, GigE at first, IB in 2010. End is a placeholder. Earlier Nagasaki clusters (256 x 8800 GTS Nov 2008, +256 9800 GTX Apr 2009) not added: config ambiguous. Vendor peak FP32 for G80/GT200 counts MAD+MUL dual-issue (3 flop/clk/SP); MAD-only = x2/3
